_preregistration.sample_size_justification: dp_pipeline_validation ladder on DK: 512 replicas reaches ~8% on both exponents and 4096/32768 barely improve on it
_preregistration.pipeline_bias: measured inline on DK at this run's own geometry, not imported
_preregistration.calibration_gate: if DK's known exponents are not recovered to 20% at N=96/40 sweeps, the geometry cannot decide and the LM result is NOT DECIDABLE regardless of its numbers
_preregistration.primary: do delta and theta agree on a single T_c inside [0.40, 0.45] at 512 replicas?
_preregistration.still_disagreeing_means: evidence against a DP reading, but ONLY if the gate passes
_preregistration.resumable: every completed run is saved immediately and keyed by (T, seed)

verdict: NOT DECIDABLE AT THIS GEOMETRY: on Domany-Kinzel, which provably IS directed percolation, this estimator at N=96 over 40 sweeps recovers delta to 21.2+/-10.0% and theta to 7.0+/-6.6%, which does not demonstrate the 20% that dp_pipeline_validation pre-registered. The LM deviations (delta {'0.4': 186.8, '0.425': 74.9, '0.45': 26.9}, theta {'0.4': 101.9, '0.425': 22.6, '0.45': 27.2}) are therefore not separable from the fit window, and the DP question cannot be answered either way from this run -- in particular the earlier 'not in the DP class' reading, which came from applying a tolerance measured at N=512/200 sweeps to a run at N=96/40, does not survive: that tolerance rejects DK itself at this geometry. N=192 over 120 sweeps does (9.8+/-8.1% / 9.2+/-5.6%), at a projected 13.8 h on this machine.

_analysis_provenance.note: sha256 of the analysis source at write time. If this does not match the file on disk, the analysis was produced by a different version of the code -- re-run it before reading the numbers (issue #38).

_note: Phase 2 of #82: narrow phase 1's theta-crossing bracket [0.40, 0.45] at 512 replicas per temperature and test whether delta and theta agree on one T_c. The sample size comes from dp_pipeline_validation's ladder on Domany-Kinzel, where the exponents are known: 512 reaches ~8% on both and 4096/32768 barely improve, so the 2000-20000 first guessed from the DP literature was 5-40x more than needed. Deviations are judged against twice the pipeline's own DK-measured bias rather than against Jensen directly, because claiming tighter agreement than the estimator demonstrably achieves on a known system would be reading noise. B=64 rather than 16 because the measurement is sequential in sweeps*N and B trades against GPU occupancy: 5.72 s per replica vs 9.63, measured. AMENDED after the first full pass: that bias was initially hardcoded from the validation run's geometry (N=512, 200 sweeps) while this runs at N=96 over 40, where the identical estimator recovers DK's delta to only ~33%. The first verdict therefore rejected DP using a tolerance that rejects DK itself. The bias is now measured inline at this run's own geometry and the DP test is gated on it -- a gate evaluated on DK alone, blind to the LM numbers -- with a geometry ladder reporting which configuration would decide and its projected cost. The 24 LM trajectories are unchanged; only the analysis was rerun.

calibration_at_run_geometry.gate: mean deviation PLUS its seed-to-seed spread must clear the tolerance
